articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities and Individuals in Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Actions
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on November 13, 2026, targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics and counter terrorism activities.
These actions aim to disrupt financial networks supporting illicit drug trafficking and terrorist organizations globally, reinforcing the U.S. commitment to combating these threats.
Further details regarding the specific individuals and entities designated, and the implications for U.S. persons, are available on the Treasury website.

This update includes modifications to existing listings and may involve new entries or changes to identifying information for previously sanctioned individuals and entities.
The action underscores the ongoing U.S. policy of applying economic pressure on Iran.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces New Iran-related Designations
body: On November 6, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations.
These designations target individuals and entities deemed to be involved in activities that support the Iranian regime or its illicit proliferation activities.
The U.S. Treasury continues to utilize sanctions to address concerns regarding Iran's nuclear program and regional destabilizing actions.

articles.headline: OFAC Targets Cyber-related and Transnational Criminal Organizations, Imposes New Cuba Sanctions, and Publishes Cuba-related Determination
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a series of designations on November 5, 2026, targeting cyber-related and transnational criminal organizations, alongside new sanctions against Cuba.

Additionally, OFAC published a Cuba-related Determination Pursuant to Section 2(a)(i)(A) of Executive Order 14404, specifically targeting the 'Electronics, Manufacturing, Marine, and Technology Sectors of the Cuban Economy.'
This action expands the scope of U.S. sanctions on Cuba, allowing for the designation of companies and individuals operating in these newly identified sectors.

body: On November 4, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and provided updates to certain existing Iran-related listings.
Concurrently, OFAC published an Iran-related alert to inform the public about potential sanctions risks.
Furthermore, an amended Venezuela-related General License and a corresponding Frequently Asked Question were issued, indicating adjustments to U.S. policy concerning Venezuela.

Parties engaging in Iran-related transactions are advised to review the amended General License for compliance.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
